ANC LOSES IT's GRIP

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the election results are announced, and the ANC bleeds, stabbed in the back by one of it's own founders, South Africa wakes up to a transformed political landscape with new hopes but high risks

Unique Selling Point:
We have an opportunity to both witness the results of the elections being announced, and explore the reasons for the dramatic shift in power, as well as start to build an analysis as to why voters have turned their backs partly on the ANC, the party which brought liberation and the promise of transformation to the country after years of apartheid and centuries of colonialism,


Summary:
In a set of dramatic election results, the ANC has lost its foothold and come crashing down by considerable margins as angry voters turn their back on the party of liberation, due to it's poor record of service delivery and the neglect of it's mandate. In this watershed election, the ANC has lost political control of three provinces: Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Northern Cape and been unable to turn around its fortunes in a fourth, the Western Cape, which has stuck, mainly with the Democratic Alliance. The loss of power comes partly as a result of a surge in popularity of the MK Party which has captured the hearts, minds and votes of the people of KwaZulu-Natal, and to a degree in Gauteng. Despite of and maybe because of the MK party's shift away from the liberal tenants and commitments of the constitution, the breakaway party has garnered support that the ANC did not believe possible. We explore why this shift has happened, and how it will shape the future of governance in South Africa for the next five years, asking to what extent it is a political and ideological move within South African society, to what extent it is show of resentment and to what extent MK's popularity is based on the cult and charisma of the wily former President, Jacob Zuma, who will not even make it to Parliament due to his criminal record.

Press Release:


A Political Purge
The African National Congress has for decades stood as a monument of liberation in South Africa and on the ballot, voters have rewarded the party with their loyalty. But with a poor record of service delivery, staggering unemployment and a rise in crime levels throughout the country, the ANC's popularity has waned. In May, in a set of dramatic election results, the ANC finally lost its foothold and came crashing down by considerable margins. The loss of faith in the ANC comes as former President Jacob Zuma capitalises on a surge of popularity for his MK Party, which has captured the hearts, minds and votes of the people of KwaZulu-Natal, and to a degree in Gauteng. It’s a catastrophic result for the humbled ANC, which forces it now to examine all options, none of which provide an easy path back to power. It must form a new government with parties that many might argue, are their traditional enemies – diametrically opposed on ideology and culture, and in some instances commitment to the constitution. For the next ten days, critical discussions will happen behind closed doors while anxious South Africans await a result. Carte Blanche examines why this shift has happened, and how it might shape the future of governance in South Africa for the next five years.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Erin Bates

Script:


ANC LOSES ITS GRIP - # 6558
FINAL SCRIPT

(VO1) IT WAS THE MOST ANTICIPATED ELECTION IN THE COUNTRY SINCE 1994…..

REBECCA DAVIS:
This has been easily the most memorable elections of the Democratic era in South Africa in 30 years…

(VO2) IT’S BEEN A CHANCE FOR A RESET….

DAN MOYANE, ENCA Anchor:
We are at a crossroads in terms of our political landscape.

(VO3) AND AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPRESS GROWING ANGER AT THE RULING PARTY, THE AFRICAN NATIONAL CONGRESS, FOR IT’S FAILURE TO DELIVER ON PROMISES FOR A BETTER LIFE FOR ALL

Junior Khumalo, Political Reporter, Newzroom Afrika:
I knew that there was a lot of frustrations on the ground. But I did not anticipate that it was this much.

(VO4) CITIZENS WERE SLOW TO REGISTER FOR THE ELECTIONS – A THIRD DIDN’T EVEN BOTHER. AND OF THOSE, ONLY 58 PER CENT ACTUALLY VOTED WHICH WAS SIGNIFICANT, ACCORDING TO POLITICAL WRITER RICHARD CALLAND.


PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND
Political Writer
The effect of this, of course, is that around legitimacy, so the ANC not only went well below 50%, but it means that around one in seven eligible voters voted for the ANC.

(VO5) OVER FOUR DAYS, THE COUNTS TRICKLED IN TO THE RESULTS CENTRE IN MIDRAND.
WHEN THE FIGURES CAME INTO FINAL FOCUS, THEY REVEALED A MONUMENTAL SHIFT.

PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND
Political Writer
What's needed is a new culture of politics where there's an acceptance that power has to be shared…The electorate has chosen this time not to give any one single party a majority.

(VO6) THE ANC CRASHED TO 40 PER CENT NATIONALLY.
THIS MEANS IT LOST SEVENTY-ONE SEATS IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. A HANDFUL OF CABINET MINISTERS WERE CASUALTIES IN THIS LANDSLIDE.

DAY ONE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera:
Even before the elections, there were clear signs that the ANC was going to take a beating.
But as the numbers came out, they still seemed to come as a shock to senior leaders.

(VO7) NONE MORE SO THAN THE STRONG PERFORMANCE OF FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA’S UMKHONTO WE SIZWE PARTY IN TRADITIONAL ANC STRONGHOLDS.

FIKILE MBLALULA from Press Conference:
You don't want to accept the reality that you lost KZN in free and fair to Jacob Zuma. You want to blame it on somebody. ….But the fact of the matter is that as we speak today, Jacob Zuma is a force to be reckoned with.

(VO8) YET THE WRITING WAS ON THE WALL, ACCORDING TO GARETH VAN ONSELEN WHO RUNS A MARKET RESEARCH COMPANY.
HIS DATA SHOWED HOW EVERYTHING CHANGED IN DECEMBER LAST YEAR WITH THE ARRIVAL OF THE MK PARTY ONTO THE POLITICAL STAGE.

GARETH VAN ONSELEN
CEO, Victory Research
DAY TWO 11: 42
We'd run a number of polls before MK was formed and the ANC seems sort of stuck between 45 and 50. But MK arrived on the scene. And we did a poll …. which put them at about 25% in KZN and it fundamentally changed the nature of the political landscape. It exploded the ANC's votes, in KZN and fractured it and from that on …and it fundamentally changed the landscape.

(VO9) GARETH’S COMPANY, VICTORY RESEARCH, TRACKED ELECTORAL SENTIMENT ALMOST IN REAL TIME.
IT WAS A SPRINT FINISH IN KWAZULU-NATAL FOR THE MK PARTY.

GARETH VAN ONSELEN
CEO, Victory Research
It took about three weeks of the tracking polll for party supporters to start to decide where their loyalties lay. I mean, the the party in the lead in KZN switched sides about five times I think before election day, MK would fight back the DA was in lead for a short period, remarkably, the ANC then overtook MK. And right till the end, those parties were fighting till the death, it was only in about the last 10 days that MK started to pull away substantially from the ANC.

(VO10)NOT ONLY BAGGING 58 SEATS IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. MK DECIMATED THE ANC IN KWAZULU-NATAL.
IT ATE UP THE EFF AND CAPPED THE IFP’S GROWTH.
ZUMA’S PARTY GRABBED 37 OUT OF 80 SEATS IN THE KZN LEGISLATURE, IN TOUCHING DISTANCE OF AN OUTRIGHT MAJORITY.

DAY ONE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera:
Former President Jacob Zuma and his party left his former comrades in the dust. And to add insult to injury, Zuma alleged that the elections were rigged.

PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND
Political Writer
I think MK is a reflection of its of its of its figurehead, its leader, Jacob Zuma. He thrives on chaos. He thrives on destabilising institutions.

(VO11) WE APPROACHED THE MK PARTY FOR COMMENT, BUT THEY HAVE YET TO RESPOND.
THE PARTY’S BOLD APPROACH IS CLEAR TO SEE IN THEIR STREAM OF SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS. AND DURING THE CAMPAIGN, PARTY AGENTS WORKED THE FIELD IN KWAZULU-NATAL, A PROVINCE WITH A LONG HISTORY OF POLITICAL VIOLENCE,

GARETH VAN ONSELEN
CEO, Victory Research13:59
MK operates almost exclusively on the ground through networking. … I imagined they would have got a lot of their strategies and tactics on the ground from the ANC, which involves going house to house, going to people's doors, communicating with communities and spreading things through word of mouth, but what they were saying and who they were talking to and how effective they were, I don't think we'll ever know.

(VO12) DESPITE YEARS WORKING IN KZN, MK’S SUCCESS AMAZED POLITICAL REPORTER, SIHLE MAVUSO.

SIHLE MAVUSO,
Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa
I never expected the MK party to go to the hostel of KwaMashu. north of Durban and win that was the outright with outright majority. The IFP has never lost that place. But the MK party went there. And they won that one. The Mk party went Msinga, an IFP stronghold for 10 years. They won that place. They went to Nongoma, they did they same, they went to Dumbe, they did the same, they say they went to Ulundi, they did the same.

ERIN BATES: So how did Mr Zuma and the MK do it?

SIHLE MAVUSO,
Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa
Part of the strategy was to appease the guys that were pushed out as a result of ANC factional fights. He also appeased the traditional, traditional leaders, he also appeased the members of the Shembe Church and he also appeased the poor, he spoke their language he was drumming hope into them, telling them that once the MK party is in power right now, I mean after the elections, everything will change.

(VO13)FORMER PRESIDENT ZUMA NOW HAS POWER TO PLAY WITH.
AND IN AN UNEXPECTED TWIST, HE TRIED TO HALT THE DECLARATION OF ELECTION RESULTS. HE WANTED A RECOUNT OR EVEN A RERUN.

Jacob Zuma Soundup: And I am hoping that whoever is responsible is hearing what we are saying: Don’t start trouble, when there is no trouble.

(VO14)THE IEC STOOD FIRM.

Mosotho Moepya, Chairperson of the IEC: The Electoral Commission of South Africa declares the results of the 2024 national and provincial elections as free and fair.

(VO15) IN A FURTHER BOOST FOR DEMOCRACY, THE ANC ACCEPTED IT’S DEVASTATING LOSS.

FIKILE MBLALULA from Press Conference:
The elections have humbled us they've brought us where we are. And therefore we've got to talk to everyone.

(VO16) THE FORMER RULING PARTY IS NOW BETWEEN A ROCK AND A HARD PLACE - HOW TO FORM A GOVERNMENT, APPEASE ITS ALLIES AND SAVE THE ECONOMY.

ERIN BATES Piece to Camera:
This is not just about party politics, this is not just about political manifestos.
This is also about the personalities who have to manage this crisis all while holding on to their positions

(VO17) SUDDENLY POLITICAL OPPONENTS ARE CONTEMPLATING COALITION AGREEMENTS THAT REQUIRE AN UNCOMFORTABLE COSINESS.
EARLY TALKS OF AN ANC - DA TIE-UP - WHICH WAS PUNTED BY BUSINESS
AND IS NO LONGER ON THE TABLE - WAS UNLIKELY TO WORK IN REALITY, SAYS POLITICAL COLUMNIST JUSTICE MALALA.

JUSTICE MALALA
Political Columnist
I think that the idea that we can have an ANC-DA coalition actually doesn't take cognizance of the fact that our history still remains very much with us. The fact that we, we went through apartheid, that we we are still racially divided in large measure, that there huge disparities in wealth and so forth between black and white, this place of such a big issue in the ANC and ANC politics. I think that there's such a pushback about that idea of going with a DA

(VO18)JUSTICE HAS BEEN TALKING TO JITTERY INVESTORS TO EXPLORE SOUTH AFRICA’S RISK. THERE IS CONCERN THAT THE COUNTRY WILL EXPERIENCE VIOLENCE, SIMILAR TO THE LOOTING THAT HAPPENED IN KZN IN 2021.

JUSTICE MALALA
Political Columnist
I think this is a very dangerous moment for South Africa. I think that you have on the one hand, a player like Jacob Zuma, who's taken on this narrative that that it's all corrupt, it's all about me me me, they were trying to stop me from the Union Buildings or wherever, he could try to undermine the system in various ways. But in the background, you can hear the noise saying we can cause havoc here….so I think that's the threat of violence, I think that there is a threat of a constitutional crisis if we don't find some way through these coalitions

(VO16)WITH THIS RECENT HISTORY, THE PEOPLE OF KWAZULU-NATAL ARE ANXIOUS TO SEE WHAT COMES NEXT.

SIHLE MAVUSO,
Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa
MK party and the EFF in one government, that will be a deadly combination. The province will be broken in three or four months time. Hence, they are saying in the province, you need to have a coalition of the DA ANC IFP and NFP, the DA has a proven track record of holding people accountable.

(VO17) TALKS ABOUT TALKS KICKED OFF AS THE RESULTS CAME IN. THE OPPOSITION PARTIES ARE ALSO GRAPPLING WITH A NEW REALITY.

JOHN STEENKAMP
Leader, Democratic Alliance
Parties within the Moonshot Pact or the Multiparty Charter, now need to ( ) make a choice about whether they're going to join hands with the constitutionalists and freedom, freedom and democracy lovers or they're going to sit it out and allow the doomsday forces who want to scrap the Constitution, nationalise banks and expropriate without compensation, get into the driving seat.

DAY THREE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera:
The first sitting of South Africa’s new Parliament will happen here at the Cape Town International Convention Centre. MPs will be sworn in and vote in a President to form a government. But already the MK party is threatening to boycott.

PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND
Political Writer
Well, it's an interesting feature of the Constitution. It has this very tight time table for for electing the president - 14 days. But then the Constitution is silent as to how long the President has to appoint his or her cabinet. So you could have a situation where there's a deal to get the presidency sorted. And then there's a second phase of negotiations around who gets what in the cabinet.

(VO18) AFTER MARATHON PARTY TALKS THIS WEEK, THE ANC EMERGED WITH A POWER SHARING ROAD MAP.

Cyril Ramaphosa: We have therefore agreed that we will invite political parties to form a Government of National Unity as the best option to move our country forward.

(VO19) THE DEVIL WILL BE IN THE DETAIL.
THE PARTY THAT HELD POWER FOR THIRTY YEARS HAS ONLY SEVEN DAYS TO GET OPPOSITION PARTIES ON BOARD.
THE CLOCK IS TICKING.

PROMO 1:

SOUTH AFRICAN POLITICIANS WALK A TIGHTROPE…
RICHARD CALLAND this is the start of a very substantial reshaping or reordering of South African politics.
(If that is too long then try: RICHARD CALLAND I think this was a freak election.)
AS THE FUTURE OF THE COUNTRY HANGS IN THE BALANCE.

PROMO 2:

THE MOST DRAMATIC ELECTIONS IN THIRTY YEARS
BUT STILL NO CLEAR OUTCOME
JUSTICE MALALA It's a free for all. So this transition is very dangerous.

PROMO 3:

THE ANC ACCEPTS IT’S ELECTORAL LOSS…
JUSTICE MALALA
More than half the people who should have voted …. just didn't pitch up
BUT STILL HOLDS THE KEYS

(VO3) AND AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPRESS GROWING ANGER AT THE RULING PARTY, THE AFRICAN NATIONAL CONGRESS, FOR IT’S FAILURE TO DELIVER ON PROMISES FOR A BETTER LIFE FOR ALL Junior Khumalo, Political Reporter, Newzroom Afrika: I knew that there was a lot of frustrations on the ground. But I did not anticipate that it was this much. (VO4) CITIZENS WERE SLOW TO REGISTER FOR THE ELECTIONS – A THIRD DIDN’T EVEN BOTHER. AND OF THOSE, ONLY 58 PER CENT ACTUALLY VOTED WHICH WAS SIGNIFICANT, ACCORDING TO POLITICAL WRITER RICHARD CALLAND. PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND Political Writer The effect of this, of course, is that around legitimacy, so the ANC not only went well below 50%, but it means that around one in seven eligible voters voted for the ANC. (VO5) OVER FOUR DAYS, THE COUNTS TRICKLED IN TO THE RESULTS CENTRE IN MIDRAND. WHEN THE FIGURES CAME INTO FINAL FOCUS, THEY REVEALED A MONUMENTAL SHIFT. PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND Political Writer What's needed is a new culture of politics where there's an acceptance that power has to be shared…The electorate has chosen this time not to give any one single party a majority. (VO6) THE ANC CRASHED TO 40 PER CENT NATIONALLY. THIS MEANS IT LOST SEVENTY-ONE SEATS IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. A HANDFUL OF CABINET MINISTERS WERE CASUALTIES IN THIS LANDSLIDE. DAY ONE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera: Even before the elections, there were clear signs that the ANC was going to take a beating. But as the numbers came out, they still seemed to come as a shock to senior leaders. (VO7) NONE MORE SO THAN THE STRONG PERFORMANCE OF FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA’S UMKHONTO WE SIZWE PARTY IN TRADITIONAL ANC STRONGHOLDS. FIKILE MBLALULA from Press Conference: You don't want to accept the reality that you lost KZN in free and fair to Jacob Zuma. You want to blame it on somebody. ….But the fact of the matter is that as we speak today, Jacob Zuma is a force to be reckoned with. (VO8) YET THE WRITING WAS ON THE WALL, ACCORDING TO GARETH VAN ONSELEN WHO RUNS A MARKET RESEARCH COMPANY. HIS DATA SHOWED HOW EVERYTHING CHANGED IN DECEMBER LAST YEAR WITH THE ARRIVAL OF THE MK PARTY ONTO THE POLITICAL STAGE. GARETH VAN ONSELEN CEO, Victory Research DAY TWO 11: 42 We'd run a number of polls before MK was formed and the ANC seems sort of stuck between 45 and 50. But MK arrived on the scene. And we did a poll …. which put them at about 25% in KZN and it fundamentally changed the nature of the political landscape. It exploded the ANC's votes, in KZN and fractured it and from that on …and it fundamentally changed the landscape. (VO9) GARETH’S COMPANY, VICTORY RESEARCH, TRACKED ELECTORAL SENTIMENT ALMOST IN REAL TIME. IT WAS A SPRINT FINISH IN KWAZULU-NATAL FOR THE MK PARTY. GARETH VAN ONSELEN CEO, Victory Research It took about three weeks of the tracking polll for party supporters to start to decide where their loyalties lay. I mean, the the party in the lead in KZN switched sides about five times I think before election day, MK would fight back the DA was in lead for a short period, remarkably, the ANC then overtook MK. And right till the end, those parties were fighting till the death, it was only in about the last 10 days that MK started to pull away substantially from the ANC. (VO10)NOT ONLY BAGGING 58 SEATS IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. MK DECIMATED THE ANC IN KWAZULU-NATAL. IT ATE UP THE EFF AND CAPPED THE IFP’S GROWTH. ZUMA’S PARTY GRABBED 37 OUT OF 80 SEATS IN THE KZN LEGISLATURE, IN TOUCHING DISTANCE OF AN OUTRIGHT MAJORITY. DAY ONE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera: Former President Jacob Zuma and his party left his former comrades in the dust. And to add insult to injury, Zuma alleged that the elections were rigged. PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND Political Writer I think MK is a reflection of its of its of its figurehead, its leader, Jacob Zuma. He thrives on chaos. He thrives on destabilising institutions. (VO11) WE APPROACHED THE MK PARTY FOR COMMENT, BUT THEY HAVE YET TO RESPOND. THE PARTY’S BOLD APPROACH IS CLEAR TO SEE IN THEIR STREAM OF SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS. AND DURING THE CAMPAIGN, PARTY AGENTS WORKED THE FIELD IN KWAZULU-NATAL, A PROVINCE WITH A LONG HISTORY OF POLITICAL VIOLENCE, GARETH VAN ONSELEN CEO, Victory Research13:59 MK operates almost exclusively on the ground through networking. … I imagined they would have got a lot of their strategies and tactics on the ground from the ANC, which involves going house to house, going to people's doors, communicating with communities and spreading things through word of mouth, but what they were saying and who they were talking to and how effective they were, I don't think we'll ever know. (VO12) DESPITE YEARS WORKING IN KZN, MK’S SUCCESS AMAZED POLITICAL REPORTER, SIHLE MAVUSO. SIHLE MAVUSO, Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa I never expected the MK party to go to the hostel of KwaMashu. north of Durban and win that was the outright with outright majority. The IFP has never lost that place. But the MK party went there. And they won that one. The Mk party went Msinga, an IFP stronghold for 10 years. They won that place. They went to Nongoma, they did they same, they went to Dumbe, they did the same, they say they went to Ulundi, they did the same. ERIN BATES: So how did Mr Zuma and the MK do it? SIHLE MAVUSO, Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa Part of the strategy was to appease the guys that were pushed out as a result of ANC factional fights. He also appeased the traditional, traditional leaders, he also appeased the members of the Shembe Church and he also appeased the poor, he spoke their language he was drumming hope into them, telling them that once the MK party is in power right now, I mean after the elections, everything will change. (VO13)FORMER PRESIDENT ZUMA NOW HAS POWER TO PLAY WITH. AND IN AN UNEXPECTED TWIST, HE TRIED TO HALT THE DECLARATION OF ELECTION RESULTS. HE WANTED A RECOUNT OR EVEN A RERUN. Jacob Zuma Soundup: And I am hoping that whoever is responsible is hearing what we are saying: Don’t start trouble, when there is no trouble. (VO14)THE IEC STOOD FIRM. Mosotho Moepya, Chairperson of the IEC: The Electoral Commission of South Africa declares the results of the 2024 national and provincial elections as free and fair. (VO15) IN A FURTHER BOOST FOR DEMOCRACY, THE ANC ACCEPTED IT’S DEVASTATING LOSS. FIKILE MBLALULA from Press Conference: The elections have humbled us they've brought us where we are. And therefore we've got to talk to everyone. (VO16) THE FORMER RULING PARTY IS NOW BETWEEN A ROCK AND A HARD PLACE - HOW TO FORM A GOVERNMENT, APPEASE ITS ALLIES AND SAVE THE ECONOMY. ERIN BATES Piece to Camera: This is not just about party politics, this is not just about political manifestos. This is also about the personalities who have to manage this crisis all while holding on to their positions (VO17) SUDDENLY POLITICAL OPPONENTS ARE CONTEMPLATING COALITION AGREEMENTS THAT REQUIRE AN UNCOMFORTABLE COSINESS. EARLY TALKS OF AN ANC - DA TIE-UP - WHICH WAS PUNTED BY BUSINESS AND IS NO LONGER ON THE TABLE - WAS UNLIKELY TO WORK IN REALITY, SAYS POLITICAL COLUMNIST JUSTICE MALALA. JUSTICE MALALA Political Columnist I think that the idea that we can have an ANC-DA coalition actually doesn't take cognizance of the fact that our history still remains very much with us. The fact that we, we went through apartheid, that we we are still racially divided in large measure, that there huge disparities in wealth and so forth between black and white, this place of such a big issue in the ANC and ANC politics. I think that there's such a pushback about that idea of going with a DA (VO18)JUSTICE HAS BEEN TALKING TO JITTERY INVESTORS TO EXPLORE SOUTH AFRICA’S RISK. THERE IS CONCERN THAT THE COUNTRY WILL EXPERIENCE VIOLENCE, SIMILAR TO THE LOOTING THAT HAPPENED IN KZN IN 2021. JUSTICE MALALA Political Columnist I think this is a very dangerous moment for South Africa. I think that you have on the one hand, a player like Jacob Zuma, who's taken on this narrative that that it's all corrupt, it's all about me me me, they were trying to stop me from the Union Buildings or wherever, he could try to undermine the system in various ways. But in the background, you can hear the noise saying we can cause havoc here….so I think that's the threat of violence, I think that there is a threat of a constitutional crisis if we don't find some way through these coalitions (VO16)WITH THIS RECENT HISTORY, THE PEOPLE OF KWAZULU-NATAL ARE ANXIOUS TO SEE WHAT COMES NEXT. SIHLE MAVUSO, Senior Political Journalist, Scrolla.Africa MK party and the EFF in one government, that will be a deadly combination. The province will be broken in three or four months time. Hence, they are saying in the province, you need to have a coalition of the DA ANC IFP and NFP, the DA has a proven track record of holding people accountable. (VO17) TALKS ABOUT TALKS KICKED OFF AS THE RESULTS CAME IN. THE OPPOSITION PARTIES ARE ALSO GRAPPLING WITH A NEW REALITY. JOHN STEENKAMP Leader, Democratic Alliance Parties within the Moonshot Pact or the Multiparty Charter, now need to ( ) make a choice about whether they're going to join hands with the constitutionalists and freedom, freedom and democracy lovers or they're going to sit it out and allow the doomsday forces who want to scrap the Constitution, nationalise banks and expropriate without compensation, get into the driving seat. DAY THREE - ERIN BATES Piece to Camera: The first sitting of South Africa’s new Parliament will happen here at the Cape Town International Convention Centre. MPs will be sworn in and vote in a President to form a government. But already the MK party is threatening to boycott. PROFESSOR RICHARD CALLAND Political Writer Well, it's an interesting feature of the Constitution. It has this very tight time table for for electing the president - 14 days. But then the Constitution is silent as to how long the President has to appoint his or her cabinet. So you could have a situation where there's a deal to get the presidency sorted. And then there's a second phase of negotiations around who gets what in the cabinet. (VO18) AFTER MARATHON PARTY TALKS THIS WEEK, THE ANC EMERGED WITH A POWER SHARING ROAD MAP. Cyril Ramaphosa: We have therefore agreed that we will invite political parties to form a Government of National Unity as the best option to move our country forward. (VO19) THE DEVIL WILL BE IN THE DETAIL. THE PARTY THAT HELD POWER FOR THIRTY YEARS HAS ONLY SEVEN DAYS TO GET OPPOSITION PARTIES ON BOARD. THE CLOCK IS TICKING. PROMO 1: SOUTH AFRICAN POLITICIANS WALK A TIGHTROPE… RICHARD CALLAND this is the start of a very substantial reshaping or reordering of South African politics. (If that is too long then try: RICHARD CALLAND I think this was a freak election.) AS THE FUTURE OF THE COUNTRY HANGS IN THE BALANCE. PROMO 2: THE MOST DRAMATIC ELECTIONS IN THIRTY YEARS BUT STILL NO CLEAR OUTCOME JUSTICE MALALA It's a free for all. So this transition is very dangerous. PROMO 3: THE ANC ACCEPTS IT’S ELECTORAL LOSS… JUSTICE MALALA More than half the people who should have voted …. just didn't pitch up BUT STILL HOLDS THE KEYS

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): As the election results are announced, and the ANC bleeds, stabbed in the back by one of it's own founders, South Africa wakes up to a transformed political landscape with new hopes but high risks
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have an opportunity to both witness the results of the elections being announced, and explore the reasons for the dramatic shift in power, as well as start to build an analysis as to why voters have turned their backs partly on the ANC, the party which brought liberation and the promise of transformation to the country after years of apartheid and centuries of colonialism,
metadata.Summary: In a set of dramatic election results, the ANC has lost its foothold and come crashing down by considerable margins as angry voters turn their back on the party of liberation, due to it's poor record of service delivery and the neglect of it's mandate. In this watershed election, the ANC has lost political control of three provinces: Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Northern Cape and been unable to turn around its fortunes in a fourth, the Western Cape, which has stuck, mainly with the Democratic Alliance. The loss of power comes partly as a result of a surge in popularity of the MK Party which has captured the hearts, minds and votes of the people of KwaZulu-Natal, and to a degree in Gauteng. Despite of and maybe because of the MK party's shift away from the liberal tenants and commitments of the constitution, the breakaway party has garnered support that the ANC did not believe possible. We explore why this shift has happened, and how it will shape the future of governance in South Africa for the next five years, asking to what extent it is a political and ideological move within South African society, to what extent it is show of resentment and to what extent MK's popularity is based on the cult and charisma of the wily former President, Jacob Zuma, who will not even make it to Parliament due to his criminal record.
